citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The attending veterinarian does not conduct regularly scheduled visits to the premises. The licensee has a formal
arrangement with an attending veterinarian and a written Program of Veterinary Care but does not have arrangements for
the attending veterinarian (AV) to conduct regularly scheduled visits to the premises. The licensee provided a Program of
Veterinary Care with the space documenting the frequency of the regularly scheduled visits by the veterinarian that states
the visits will be conducted on an annual basis. The attending veterinarian has not conducted a site visit at the facility in
the last year according to the facility representative.
Without the required regularly scheduled visits to the premises, the attending veterinarian cannot effectively ensure the
provision of adequate veterinary care and the health and well-being of the animals housed at the facility.
Each dealer and exhibitor shall employ an attending veterinarian under formal arrangements. In the case of a part-time
attending veterinarian or consultant arrangements, the formal arrangements shall include a written program of veterinary
care and regularly scheduled visits to the premises of the dealer or exhibitor.
Correct by 21-October- 2026

The facility does not have an effective program of pest control for flies. There are 6 primary enclosures housing 7 striped
skunks that were observed with too numerous to count flies flying around and inside of the primary enclosures. A primary
enclosure was observed with a pool of thick brown liquid that contained multiple live maggots crawling through the liquid.
Additionally, a second primary enclosure was observed with a pile of feces just on the outside of the enclosure with live
maggots crawling through the fecal material.
Flies and other insects can harbor and transmit disease, contaminate food and water, and cause discomfort and distress
to the animals. The facility must establish and maintain an effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and
avian and mammalian pests.
Correct by 5-October-2026.
This is a continuation of the report for the routine inspection conducted on 21-September-2026 and contains the
remaining non-compliances found during the inspection. The exit briefing for the items included on this report was
conducted on 22-September-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
